title: ChatGPT Desktop browser facade uses a local stdio MCP plugin
summary: For CT-03, the supported local path is ChatGPT Desktop Codex/OWL -> local plugin -> stdio MCP process -> loopback companion ingress -> Chrome adapter -> explicitly shared pages.
claims: An HTTP MCP configured at 127.0.0.1 can appear in the Codex MCP registry without becoming a ChatGPT conversation tool surface.
A Desktop plugin can launch a local MCP process through .mcp.json command/args.
The local stdio facade exports only list_tabs, read_page, find_in_page and bridge_status.
decision: Use the local stdio MCP facade as the canonical CT-03 Desktop transport; keep /mcp/browser for OAuth/HTTP compatibility and diagnostics.
rationale: This keeps execution local, preserves explicit Chrome sharing, avoids remote localhost registration, and matches working Desktop plugin packaging patterns.

evidence.note: Harness suite passed after local ingress changes.

evidence.ref: MCP SDK bridge_status through stdio facade
